notes: The live camera used to show only the skeleton on a black screen: the live view drew the rig but never the video of you underneath it, trusting the phone to show the camera picture behind the lines — and on your phone that picture stayed black even while the skeleton tracked you. The live view now paints the camera picture under the skeleton, using the same alignment as the lines, so you see yourself with the rig on you — before the pose even locks on, so you can get into frame. When the camera isn't ready yet it still draws just the lines, like before.

Block starts now get a Set position photo in the deep check: the last still frame of you in the blocks before the drive — the exact frame the first-movement time is measured from — with the rig drawn on it and the video frame underneath, labelled with how long after that frame you first moved. A start with no still set shows no photo, never a neighbour's.

Best and worst photos are no longer blurry quarter-size copies: they are captured at the video's own resolution (up to 1080p), keep the clip's own shape with no black bars, and have the rig drawn on top. The live fallback when the rig engine is missing paints the video frame under the bones too, so the rig is never floating on black in any view.
